posts.title: Wizarding World 2026 - Rumors & Discussion
posts.text: It's not just that they're newer. I was talking about both sales discounts and critical reception. The SW ones got a lot of criticism for a) the bad sound quality and b) the poor builds. SW fans as a rule are quite picky about, well, everything, and demand 100% movies accuracy, so issues like a spaceship not having the right lines due to having to accommodate the Smart Brick, having a hole in it when you take the Smart Brick out, or Darth Vader sounding nothing like himself didn't go over at all well. The Pokemon ones were much better received. The way Pokemons "talk" just seems to work better with the Smart Brick's limited capabilities, and the cube shape they've come up with for the builds hides the Smart Brick quite effectively. Yeah that was my point, they originally did test it with City, and City has a number of possible use cases that wouldn't involve fighting (emergency vehicles and the like). But so far what they've released is mostly SW vehicles shooting at each other and Pokemon fighting each other and next year I guess we'll get Ninjago mechs and/or dragons fighting each other. Which is why I don't expect them to branch out into Smart Play HP just now.

posts.title: Help with finding solutions for getting an AT-AT walk cycle like in the movies.
posts.text: New part offerings have been a godsend throughout the project, so I probably won't pass up something I feel enhances the model. Things like the perpendicular-hole liftarms that have come out in the past 5 years made the current version a reality that couldn't have existed when I started. There's no way I could have reached this point without reevaluating the design to utilize new parts. I started with two Power Functions motors, an infared sensor, a reverse polarity switch, and a battery pack. That stuff took up so much space. The Powered Up motor freed up tons of space and weight. I'll post some new photos and video soon. I found a way to get the stepping motions bolder. There was some subtle rubbing between a few chassis parts that I'd deemed acceptable for several months, but reevaluated today and found a way to eliminate it. Those few tenths of a millimeter equated to a decent amount of lift and stride when compounded down through the legs. I'm working through a dozen or so more details and also playing around with generating instructions. After that, I'll gather parts to do a test build off my own instructions. Then I have a friend who will proof it out with a test build. I'm also planning to do a photo/video session with a miniature snow set for promotion and possible packaging. I haven't decided if I want to do Rebrickable or make actual sets. I don't like how cheap models sell for on Rebrickable. Maybe I'm overly proud of my model, but $40 just doesn't feel like nearly enough. That's about the most expensive instructions I see on there. I did a test wanted list on Bricklink to see what sourcing the 2000 or so parts would be. Probably around $600 US dollars, so if I sold a complete set, it would be pricey, even after sourcing the cheapest possible parts. Any opinions on Rebrickable versus actual sets?

posts.title: [MOC] UT/F-150 Raptor Shuttle
posts.text: The legendary UT/F-150 Raptor was first developed in 2620, marking the debut of Holy Drives Industries, a little-known manufacturer based in the colonies. A complex and expensive manufacturing process meant that it was a commercial failure at first. But when the Great War began, demand surged. Hundreds of thousands of “Raptors” began rolling off the production lines. The versatility of the design and numerous available variants gave the machine an exceptionally wide range of uses. The shuttle proved itself in the atmospheres of numerous planets as well as in the vacuum of space. The “Raptors” served on practically every front of the war. They transported troops, provided fire support for infantry, delivered supplies, and evacuated the wounded. It was hard to find a single major battle in which these machines had not played a part. And it was the “Raptors” that proudly led the flypast at the victory parade celebrating the war's end. But peacetime was far less kind to them. Millions of shuttles, so desperately needed just a short time before, were simply left behind at military bases, in the hangars of remote colonies. Yet the story of the UT/F-150 did not end there. Colonists refurbished the abandoned shuttles, converted them for civilian use, and put them back to work. Easy to maintain and remarkably resilient, the “Raptors” found their place in all corners of settled space. It seemed as if the legendary vehicles would live out their final years rebuilding worlds broken by war. ...but then came the Guild Wars. And once again, the “Raptor” found itself where it was needed most. (see some more renders on Flickr)

posts.title: Marvel Superheroes 2026 - Rumors & Discussion
posts.text: It's difficult because that was one of their best shows (I would say it goes Loki, vision quest, a sizable gap, Moon Knight, wandavision, a sizeable gap, and then the rest) but it's also a terrible adaption of Moon Knight as a character. His powers are wrong, Jake and Steven's personalities are wrong, it's almost exclusively focused on egyptian mythology when very few of his stories actually have that much of a focus on it (the only one I can think of was created after the show to tie into it and retcon his backstory/Scarlet Scarab's existence into canon), etc. I mean... delaying secret wars is feasible (though most leakers are claiming marvel still thinks they can meet the december 2027 date - presumably this is because a lot of actors have filmed lines/scenes for secret wars during doomsday) but splitting it into two movies is fairly out there when doomsday/secret wars is essentially already the "story split into two movies". It's what they did for infinity war and endgame- one is the tragedy, the second is undoing the tragedy. I'm sure you could pad Secret Wars out to five hours of screentime if you just give more and more side characters longer stories (though I don't think they should) but I don't think those movies would have any chance of standing on their own if you were to chop it in half. Again, I think this is fairly unlikely. The same leakers who seemingly know about doomsday wave 2 sets called these secret wars sets. And of course the fact that these sets are october also heavily implies they're secret wars if the name wasn't enough. New doomsday footage- the MLB thing and a 30 second promo. The baseball one is particularly interesting as that's definitely using some actual movie shots mixed in with the MLB player shots, and there was a fairly major plot leak that involved Reed, Johnny, and Thing being at a baseball game. Which makes that leak seem very much real - the 30 second spot also has Steve and Thor take off with the Bifrost, which would imply the Also, my goat gets a line in the promo (the "I was also Cap for a minute")- I do like how they seemingly handle it, it feels like the writers are just going "look, there's a bunch of 'em now, everybody's Captain America, ok?"

posts.title: [MOC] 42145 B Model - Flight Control Set
posts.text: Since 42145 is all about aircraft controls, it is only fitting that its alternate model should revolve around the same concept. Combine that with my penchant for mini models, and voila! MINI AIRCRAFTS I chose to do 3 different types of aircrafts to increase playability. The seaplane is intended to be a mini 42040, as a homage to the first aircraft set I bought after returning to Lego (2015) and also the set that taught me about flight controls. The jet is based on the 42040 B Model, with the twin tails taken from 42066 Air Race Jet, and the function taken from 42044. Since there is only one pair of small wheels, the front wheel of the jet has to use the Bionicle ball instead. The helicopter is just a generic design that reuses the 3x3 disc as a fenestron. All three of them have connection interfaces that allow them to fit on the bars on the control set. CONTROL SET The control set use the same principles in the main model and is based on the layout of a plane's cockpit. There are three levers that control three different movements of an airplane. The joystick allows the plane to roll and pitch. The two pedals allow the plane to yaw. The side lever is intended to be the collective pitch control, which lifts the whole aircraft through changing the angle of attack. DEMONSTRATION INSTRUCTION https://reb.li/m/281305

posts.title: Prototyping Pins Using Dowels
posts.text: I got some of my 3rd party brand pins sanded down , but its slow so I need to find a better method These are for prototyping models, they make it easier to modify stuff because they can be pushed or pulled out since they don't have the stop rings however I'm also designing a standard for building that tries to ensure they can be pulled or pushed out by prioritizing pinholes or empty space on at least one side of the pin 2L axle pins 99% of the time, won't need prototyping variants, because pins cannot go thru axle holes anyway It should be easy enough to take an assembly apart enough using these brown/green prototyping pins to remove axle pins anyway But if needs must then I guess a 2L bar + stud-pin is almost like a 2L axle pin And if the stud is in the way then either a 1L pneumatic hose with a 2L rigid hose inserted 2L pin with 1L axle (11214) can be replicated with 2 parts , a bar 2L and a friction less 2L pin or the brown 2L prototyping pin - frictionless prevents the bar going too far in that's all For a 2L axle with 1L pin (18651/65249) we're back to using stud-pins and 3L bars assuming you're using this in a pinhole - axle-hole - axle-hole rather than a pinhole - pinhole -axle hole If not than you just use a 2Lpin with 1L axle part (11214), or the substitution I mentioned
